newsitem.title: GERMANY: Merged German bank seeks over 15% return on equity.
newsitem.headline: Merged German bank seeks over 15% return on equity.

text.p: Germany's new merged bank -- Bayerische Hypo- und Vereinsbank AG -- intends to aim for a return of at least 15 percent on its equity, Bayerische Vereinsbank said.
The new bank will be created, subject to cartel office approval, in a merger of Vereinsbank and Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechselbank.
Eberhard Martini, the chief executive of Hypo-Bank, gave assurances at a news conference that the new bank would have no single majority shareholder.
Martini added that the new bank would seize opportunities for acquisitions to strengthen its investment banking activities.
Asked if the new bank would consider acquisitions abroad to expand investment banking, he said: "If we see a good acquisition in our core business field, we will go ahead."
Albrecht Schmidt, chief executive of Bayerische Vereinsbank, said the merged bank would strongly expand its corporate finance business, which is primarily geared towards medium-sized companies.
He also said the new bank would seek to expand its assets management business.
